checked.what: A favorable approximate projector gives a product state with good overlap
checked.note: Proved as stated for a unique ground state; the product state is constructed, not assumed.

checked.what: A favorable approximate projector bounds the entropy by a constant times log D
checked.note: Proved directly with the explicit bound S ≤ 4 log D, without the general entropy lemma.

entries.result: Lemma 2.3, entropy from a projector and a product overlap
entries.title: The general entropy bound fails for small shrinking
entries.summary: The printed entropy bound fails on a two-qubit example; a corrected bound with an additive log D term is proved. The area-law corollary used in the rest of the paper is unaffected.
entries.context: An approximate ground-state projector K fixes the ground state Γ, multiplies the squared norm of every vector orthogonal to Γ by at most Δ, and has operator Schmidt rank at most D across the cut. Together with a product state of overlap μ with Γ, it is meant to bound the entanglement entropy S of Γ across the cut.
entries.claims: Lemma 2.3 (lines 339–348 of the source) states S ≤ O(log μ−1/log Δ−1) log D, with an absolute constant in the O.
entries.found: Let Γ be a Bell state of two qubits, the ground state of H = 1 − |Γ⟩⟨Γ|, and Ks = s + (1 − s)|Γ⟩⟨Γ| for small s > 0. Then Δ = s2, D = 4, the product state |00⟩ has μ = 1/√2, and S = log 2, while the printed right-hand side tends to zero as s → 0. All parameters are positive, the ground state is unique and the shrinking bound is attained.
entries.impact: None for the area law: the corollary S ≤ O(1) log D when DΔ ≤ 1/2, which the rest of the paper uses, is consistent with the example and is proved with S ≤ 4 log D.
entries.plan: The replacement S ≤ 12(1 + log μ−1/log Δ−1) log D, for 0 < Δ < 1, is proved for a unique ground state, together with S ≤ log D when Δ = 0. The note keeps the counterexample to the printed form.

entries.result: Lemma 4.2, interpolation and the count of collected words
entries.title: Interpolation needs only a spanning family, and one more word
entries.summary: Two small slips in the proof of the rank lemma: the interpolation needs a spanning family rather than a basis, and the count of collected words carries an extra one. Both corrections are proved, and so is the lemma.
entries.context: The rank bound for a polynomial of the Hamiltonian groups the words in the expansion of Hℓ by how often each term occurs. Each group is recovered from evaluations of a generating polynomial in commuting variables, and the words with exactly k occurrences of one window term Hi are collected into products Aa0Bb0Hi ⋯ HiAakBbk, where A and B collect the terms left and right of Hi.
entries.claims: Lines 637–643 of the source say that suitable evaluations of the generating polynomial form a basis of the space spanned by the coefficient operators, and lines 651 and 657 count binom(ℓ + k, 2k + 1) collected words.
entries.found: The coefficient operators need not be linearly independent, so the evaluations can only be required to span; spanning is all the proof uses. The collected words are indexed by 2k + 2 nonnegative exponents with sum ℓ − k, which gives binom(ℓ + k + 1, 2k + 1): already for k = 0 there are ℓ + 1 words AaBℓ−a, not ℓ. The same count appears in the two-cut version of Arad, Landau, Vazirani and Vidick.
entries.impact: None. The corrections change no exponent of the lemma.
entries.plan: Both corrections are proved, and the lemma is proved with explicit constants: rank at most (d(ℓ + 1))16(⌊ℓ/s⌋ + ⌊√ℓ⌋ + 1) for every polynomial of degree at most ℓ.

entries.result: Theorem 6.1, constants of the robustness theorem
entries.title: Constants in the robustness theorem
entries.summary: Nothing in the robustness theorem is wrong; a shift denominator, a squared cross term and a coefficient in the proof are corrected, and the theorem is proved with explicit constants.
entries.context: The robustness theorem compares the Hamiltonian H of the chain with its truncation H(t), in which the two exterior blocks are capped at height t. Before truncating, constants are subtracted from the terms so that the exterior blocks and the middle of the window have ground energy zero and H has ground energy between 0 and 6.
entries.claims: Section 6.1 shifts each of the middle terms H4, …, Hs−3 by d/(s − 7), where d is their joint ground energy. The proof of Lemma 6.5 bounds the square of a cross term by 2√(⟨v, H(t)v⟩/t), and the proof of Lemma 6.6 sums its commutator series to 4 while stating the coefficient 2.
entries.found: The range 4 ≤ i ≤ s − 3 has s − 6 terms, so the printed shift makes the middle ground energy −d/(s − 7) instead of zero; the shift is d/(s − 6), or d subtracted once from the whole middle sum. The Cauchy–Schwarz step bounds the cross term itself, not its square, by 2√(⟨v, H(t)v⟩/t). Replacing each boundary term h by h − 1/2, which has norm at most 1/2, recovers the coefficient 2. The proof of Lemma 6.6(1) writes ε for ε0.
entries.impact: None. The corrected steps give the printed conclusions.
entries.plan: The theorem is proved from the original nearest-neighbour terms: the gap of the truncated Hamiltonian is at least ε/2 and its ground state is within squared distance e−t/16 of Γ once t ≥ 32768(6 + ε)/ε2. The weight of Γ above height t is bounded by 2e−(t−20)/8 directly, without the paper's shell-by-shell induction.

entries.result: Theorem 6.1, windows of at least six terms
entries.title: Robustness for windows of at least six terms
entries.summary: Nothing is wrong with the paper; the robustness theorem is proved for windows of at least six terms, which is all the area law uses, and windows with fewer terms remain to be stated separately.
entries.context: The window around the cut has s nearest-neighbour terms. Six of them play special roles in the normalization and the truncation: the three nearest each exterior block. The area-law argument chooses s of order log2 d/ε with a large constant.
entries.claims: Theorem 6.1 (lines 949–963 of the source) states, for t of order (1/ε)(ε0/ε + 1), that the truncated Hamiltonian keeps a gap of order ε and has a ground state within 2−Ω(t) of Γ. It names no lower bound on s.
entries.found: The proof needs the six special terms to be distinct, so s ≥ 6. With s ≥ 6 the theorem is proved with explicit constants: for t ≥ (1024/ε)(ε0/ε + 1), and also for the smaller threshold t ≥ 1024 + 16 log(1/ε), the gap is at least 9ε/10 and the squared distance at most e−t/16/100. The note also records that the source's left block includes the site next to the window, that the initial product overlap at line 1023 is printed with ≤ for ≥, and that the Schmidt ranks in the sequence of Lemma 6.3 multiply rather than add.
entries.impact: None for the area law and the matrix product state approximation, whose windows have at least 21 terms. The area-law bounds keep a logarithm of 1/ε and assume that ε is the distance to the next eigenvalue.
entries.plan: State and prove the theorem for windows with fewer than six terms, which needs a different arrangement of the special terms.

entries.result: Section 5, matrix product states for frustration-free chains
entries.title: The frustration-free bond dimension needs a factor log log n
entries.summary: The printed bond dimension exp(O(ε−1/3 log2/3 n)) drops a logarithm that the paper's own rank lemma keeps; the bound with log2/3 n log log n is proved.
entries.context: For a frustration-free chain with a unique ground state Γ and gap ε, a state of constant overlap with Γ is improved by an approximate ground-state projector, a Chebyshev polynomial of degree ℓ = s2 of the truncated Hamiltonian, until it is within 1/poly(n) of Γ at every cut.
entries.claims: Lines 862–870 state that Γ is within 1/poly(n) of a matrix product state of bond dimension exp(O(ε−1/3 log2/3 n)), using Δ = e−cε−1/2s3/2 and rank D = exp(s log d).
entries.found: The exponent of ε at line 867 is +1/2, as at line 835; the minus sign is a misprint. Lemma 4.2 (line 590) gives rank (dℓ)O(ℓ/s), which is exp(O(s(log d + log s))) at ℓ = s2, and the count is sharp for the method. Line 868 drops the log s, which is of order log log n. The starting rank exp(O(log3 d/ε)) is also omitted.
entries.impact: The bond dimension is still sub-polynomial and strictly smaller than the general exp(Õ(log3/4 n/ε1/4)), but the printed rate is not derived.
entries.plan: Proved with log B ≤ C[u3/ε + (z2/ε)1/3(u + log(z + 1))], where u = 1 + log d + log(1/ε) and z = log(2048(n + 1)/δ2).
